items.followUp: Two algorithms solve the same problem. What factors would you compare to decide which one is more efficient? Give an example.

rubric.why: Identifies time and memory use as measures of efficiency.
rubric.description: Compare the algorithms’ running time and memory requirements.
rubric.how: Award for naming both time and memory (or equivalent terms).

rubric.why: An efficient algorithm must still solve the problem correctly.
rubric.description: Check that each algorithm produces the correct result.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning correctness.

rubric.why: A comparison of two algorithms makes the explanation concrete.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as linear search versus binary search.
rubric.how: Award for naming a valid pair of alternative algorithms.

rubric.why: Shows how the choice depends on the input and the algorithm’s requirements.
rubric.description: Explains that binary search is faster for a large, sorted list, while linear search can be used on an unsorted list.
rubric.how: Award for a valid comparison that links the input conditions to the choice.

modelAnswer: Compare the algorithms’ running time and memory use, while ensuring that each produces the correct result.
For example, binary search is faster than linear search on a large, sorted list.
However, binary search requires sorted data; linear search can be used on an unsorted list.
Choose the algorithm that is correct and uses less time and memory for the given problem and input.

items.followUp: Give two ways encryption helps keep everyday internet use secure.

rubric.why: Describes how encryption changes information into a coded form.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption converts readable data into coded data.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the change from readable/plaintext to coded/ciphertext or equivalent.

rubric.why: Identifies the protection encryption provides against outsiders.
rubric.description: States that encryption prevents unauthorized people from reading data.
rubric.how: Award for a clear reference to preventing unauthorized access or reading intercepted data.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant everyday internet example.
rubric.description: Mentions a use such as online banking or online payments.
rubric.how: Award for one valid everyday example.

rubric.why: Shows the kinds of information protected in daily internet use.
rubric.description: Mentions protection of personal information, passwords, or private messages.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least one relevant kind of information.

modelAnswer: Encryption converts readable information (plaintext) into coded information (ciphertext).
It helps prevent unauthorized people from reading data if it is intercepted.
It protects everyday online activities such as banking and making payments.
It also helps keep personal information, passwords, and private messages private.

items.followUp: What does the Act it Out strategy help us do when solving a problem?

rubric.why: Captures the idea of acting out or simulating a problem’s steps.
rubric.description: Defines Act it Out as physically acting out or simulating the steps of a problem or process.
rubric.how: Award for describing a simulation or physical enactment of the steps.

rubric.why: States the purpose of using the strategy.
rubric.description: Explains that acting out helps understand or solve the problem.
rubric.how: Award for stating a relevant problem-solving purpose.

modelAnswer: Act it Out is a problem-solving strategy in which we physically act out or simulate the steps of a problem.
It helps us understand the process and find a solution.

items.followUp: What is the use of a flow-line in a flowchart?

rubric.why: Identifies what the connector links in a flowchart.
rubric.description: States that a connector links parts or symbols of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the connection between flowchart parts.

rubric.why: Explains how connectors indicate continuation of the flowchart.
rubric.description: States that a connector shows where the flow continues, including between separated sections or pages.
rubric.how: Award for explaining continuation or linking separated parts.

modelAnswer: A connector symbol links separated parts of a flowchart.
It shows where the flow continues, for example when the flowchart is continued elsewhere on the page or on another page.

rubric.why: Identifies the exact text displayed by the body content.
rubric.description: Gives the displayed text: “I am student”.
rubric.how: Award for the correct text, regardless of whether the student writes it in italics.

rubric.why: Recognizes the effect of the HTML italic tag.
rubric.description: States that the displayed text is italicized.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the italic formatting.

modelAnswer: The browser displays: *I am student* (in italics).

rubric.why: Checks that the binary digits are grouped into two four-bit nibbles.
rubric.description: Groups the binary number as 1100 0001.
rubric.how: Award for the correct four-bit grouping.

rubric.why: Checks the hexadecimal conversion of both nibbles.
rubric.description: Gives the hexadecimal result C1.
rubric.how: Award for the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Group the binary digits into four-bit groups: (11000001)₂ = (1100 0001)₂.

rubric.why: Identifies whether stored data is retained.
rubric.description: States that non-volatile memory retains its stored data.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning that data is kept or retained.

rubric.why: Specifies that retention continues when power is removed.
rubric.description: States that the data remains even when the power is switched off or removed.
rubric.how: Award for explicitly linking data retention with power being off or removed.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory is memory that retains its stored data even when the power is switched off or removed.

items.followUp: Give an example of a proposition and state its truth value.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a proposition from a question or command.
rubric.description: Defines a proposition as a declarative statement.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a statement or declarative sentence.

rubric.why: States the defining property of a proposition in logic.
rubric.description: Explains that a proposition has a truth value: true or false.
rubric.how: Award for explicitly stating that it is either true or false.

modelAnswer: A proposition is a declarative statement that has a truth value.
It is either true or false.
